intent: Full-length revision of the desktop agent editor to explain per-agent MCP connection access.

image.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / precise-object-edit
Asset type: full-length desktop product screenshot concept for Dispatch's agent editor.
Edit target: the supplied desktop editor image. Keep its Dispatch brand, navy rail, pale Agents sidebar, white main surface, typography, name/description, large Instructions field, compact model summary, and capabilities section. Preserve the simple hierarchy. Extend the canvas downward substantially to give MCP access a complete, readable section. This is a LONG DESKTOP PAGE capture, roughly 1536 pixels wide and 2100 pixels tall, not a mobile layout or a collage. Maintain generous readable type instead of shrinking the whole form. No device frame.

Outside the application, a small title reads "Dispatch · Agent editor with MCP access". This is a proposed interface, not an actual access grant.

TOP EDITOR
Keep breadcrumb Agents / Recovery Engineer, title Edit definition, subtitle Reusable expertise for any project.
State: Based on revision 3 · Unsaved changes.
Keep the identity inputs and large Instructions textarea exactly as in the reference. Keep the collapsed Model row GPT-6 Astra · High. Keep Files and commands selected and Archive inspection unavailable in Capabilities.
The left rail must contain ONLY Dispatch D, Chats, Agents selected, and Settings at the bottom. Sidebar remains Agents with New agent and Recovery Engineer, Archivist, Evidence Reviewer, Developer. No invented app destinations.

REPLACE THE OLD READ-ONLY CONNECTIONS ROW WITH THIS LARGE SECTION:
Heading "MCP connections" aligned left, outlined secondary "+ Add connection" button aligned right.
Helper: "Choose which services this agent can access."
An understated text link on the next line: "Register or authenticate a server in Settings → Connections".
Show a full-width bordered connection card representing a draft selection, with a pale tinted header:
database/book icon, title "Palm Wiki", and amber outlined badge "Pending addition". This badge is about access for this agent.
Within card:
row label "MCP server" with selected server name "Palm Wiki"; below in small readable type "https://wiki.chrisreynolds.me/mcp". To the right a green dot and "Server connected". Make server connectivity clearly distinct from pending agent access.
row label "Agent identity" with a select "Recovery Engineer".
helper below identity: "This is the identity the wiki will see."
A read-only access summary labeled "Access provided by this identity":
"Articles: read and write"
"Conversation evidence: read"
small lock icon and text "Permissions are enforced by the server."
No editable permission toggles and NO credentials/password fields.

A clearly expanded disclosure labeled "Available tools · 9", with a clean compact two-column table:
Friendly name | Tool
"Search articles" | "wiki.search"
"Read articles" | "wiki.read"
"Article history" | "wiki.history"
"Find conversations" | "wiki.traceSearch"
"List conversations" | "wiki.traces"
"Read conversation" | "wiki.trace"
"Read attachment" | "wiki.file"
"Preview article edits" | "wiki.preview"
"Save articles" | "wiki.save"
Friendly names are primary; monospace tool identifiers quieter. This is information, not nine independent permission switches. All nine rows visible.

At bottom of the same card, a grouped choice titled "Apply access when saved":
selected radio "New agent instances only"
unselected radio "New and existing agent instances"
one helper "Existing instances keep their current model and instructions."
Subtle secondary text action "Remove pending connection".

BELOW THE CARD
A calm pale-blue information strip, exact text:
"Saving creates revision 4 and adds the pending connection for new instances. Existing instances are unchanged."
BOTTOM PAGE ACTION BAR:
Left secondary "Discard changes". Right ONLY teal primary "Save changes".
The complete MCP connection configuration and bottom save bar must be fully visible in the full-length image. No overlapping sticky bar.
This design stages the connection until the overall save; do not show the agent access as already granted. The green Connected status refers only to the server.
No project assignment form on this page. No workflow, runner, generic memory policy, readiness check, numbered badges, giant explanatory callouts, or repeated proposal labels. Do not introduce another competing primary action. Keep all spelling and technical tool identifiers exact. Preserve an opaque background and the polished restrained appearance of the reference.
